natural: please take care of this / please handle this / please go ahead
why_en: 'Do the needful' is understood only in South Asia. Native speakers find it vague and old-fashioned. Say exactly what you want done.
why_hi: 'Do the needful' सिर्फ़ दक्षिण एशिया में समझा जाता है। अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले इसे अस्पष्ट और पुराना मानते हैं। साफ़ कहें कि क्या करना है।
example_wrong: Kindly do the needful and revert.
example_right: Could you approve the request and let me know once it's done?

natural: reply / get back to me / respond
why_en: In standard English 'revert' means to return to a previous state (e.g. revert a commit). It never means 'reply'. 'Revert back' is doubly redundant.
why_hi: मानक अंग्रेज़ी में 'revert' का मतलब पिछली स्थिति में लौटना है (जैसे कमिट रिवर्ट करना)। इसका मतलब 'जवाब देना' कभी नहीं होता। 'Revert back' में 'back' भी फ़ालतू है।
example_wrong: Please revert back at the earliest.
example_right: Please get back to me as soon as you can.

natural: bring forward / move up / reschedule to an earlier time
why_en: 'Prepone' is Indian English only. It is logical but native speakers do not use it and may not understand it.
why_hi: 'Prepone' सिर्फ़ भारतीय अंग्रेज़ी में है। यह तर्कसंगत लगता है लेकिन अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले इसे इस्तेमाल नहीं करते और शायद न समझें।
example_wrong: Can we prepone the meeting to 2 pm?
example_right: Can we bring the meeting forward to 2 pm?

natural: please / could you / would you mind
why_en: 'Kindly' at the start of every request sounds stiff, and in emails it can read as an order dressed up as politeness. 'Please' or 'could you' is warmer.
why_hi: हर अनुरोध में 'kindly' लगाना कठोर लगता है, और ईमेल में यह विनम्रता के आवरण में आदेश जैसा पढ़ा जाता है। 'Please' या 'could you' ज़्यादा सहज है।
example_wrong: Kindly share the report. Kindly confirm.
example_right: Could you share the report and confirm when it's sent?

natural: out of town / away / travelling
why_en: 'Station' meant a colonial posting. Today native speakers hear a railway station and get confused.
why_hi: 'Station' का मतलब औपनिवेशिक काल की पोस्टिंग था। आज अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले इसे रेलवे स्टेशन समझकर भ्रमित होते हैं।
example_wrong: I will be out of station next week.
example_right: I'll be out of town next week.

natural: discuss / talk about
why_en: 'Discuss' already contains the idea of 'about'. You discuss something; you talk about something.
why_hi: 'Discuss' में ही 'about' का भाव शामिल है। 'Discuss something' या 'talk about something' कहें।
example_wrong: Let's discuss about the plan.
example_right: Let's discuss the plan.

natural: cousin
why_en: English 'cousin' has no gender and no 'brother/sister' attached. If gender matters, say 'my cousin, she...'.
why_hi: अंग्रेज़ी 'cousin' में लिंग नहीं होता और 'brother/sister' नहीं जुड़ता। लिंग बताना हो तो 'my cousin, she...' कहें।
example_wrong: My cousin brother lives in Pune.
example_right: My cousin lives in Pune.

natural: graduated / finished my degree
why_en: In standard English 'pass out' means to faint. Saying you passed out from IIT makes people picture you unconscious.
why_hi: मानक अंग्रेज़ी में 'pass out' का मतलब बेहोश होना है। 'I passed out from IIT' सुनकर लोग आपको बेहोश समझेंगे।
example_wrong: I passed out in 2017.
example_right: I graduated in 2017.

natural: this morning / last night
why_en: English pairs 'this' with today's parts and 'last' with yesterday's: this morning, this evening, last night, yesterday morning.
why_hi: अंग्रेज़ी में आज के हिस्सों के साथ 'this' और कल के साथ 'last' आता है: this morning, this evening, last night, yesterday morning।
example_wrong: I called him today morning.
example_right: I called him this morning.

natural: I'm Balvant / My name is Balvant
why_en: 'Myself' is a reflexive pronoun (I hurt myself). It cannot start an introduction.
why_hi: 'Myself' एक निजवाचक सर्वनाम है (I hurt myself)। इससे परिचय शुरू नहीं होता।
example_wrong: Myself Balvant, working as security engineer.
example_right: I'm Balvant. I work as a security engineer.

natural: it / this / that / them
why_en: 'Please find the same attached' is legal-style Indian English. Use a normal pronoun: 'Please find it attached' or better, 'I've attached it'.
why_hi: 'Please find the same attached' क़ानूनी शैली की भारतीय अंग्रेज़ी है। सामान्य सर्वनाम इस्तेमाल करें: 'I've attached it'।
example_wrong: Please review the same and confirm.
example_right: Please review it and confirm.

natural: update (noun) / updating
why_en: 'Updation' is not an English word. The noun is simply 'update'.
why_hi: 'Updation' अंग्रेज़ी शब्द नहीं है। संज्ञा बस 'update' है।
example_wrong: The updation of records is pending.
example_right: The records still need updating. / The update is pending.

natural: What's your name? / May I have your name?
why_en: A direct translation of 'आपका शुभ नाम'. English has no 'good name'; the polite form is 'May I have your name?'.
why_hi: 'आपका शुभ नाम' का सीधा अनुवाद। अंग्रेज़ी में 'good name' नहीं होता; विनम्र रूप है 'May I have your name?'।
example_wrong: What is your good name, sir?
example_right: May I have your name, please?

natural: years ago
why_en: 'Ago' is the standard word for time before now. 'Back' is only used informally in a few phrases ('a while back') and sounds odd with numbers.
why_hi: 'Ago' अतीत के समय के लिए मानक शब्द है। 'Back' सिर्फ़ कुछ अनौपचारिक वाक्यांशों में आता है और संख्या के साथ अजीब लगता है।
example_wrong: I joined this company five years back.
example_right: I joined this company five years ago.

natural: I have a question / I'm not sure about something
why_en: Two problems: 'have' for possession is not used in the continuous, and 'doubt' in English means disbelief, not a question.
why_hi: दो समस्याएँ: स्वामित्व के लिए 'have' का continuous रूप नहीं बनता, और अंग्रेज़ी में 'doubt' का मतलब अविश्वास है, सवाल नहीं।
example_wrong: Sir, I am having one doubt.
example_right: I have a question.

natural: order
why_en: 'Order' takes a direct object. You order a pizza; you do not order for a pizza. ('Order for someone' means on their behalf.)
why_hi: 'Order' सीधा कर्म लेता है। 'Order a pizza' सही है; 'order for a pizza' ग़लत। ('Order for someone' का मतलब किसी की ओर से ऑर्डर करना है।)
example_wrong: Let's order for some food.
example_right: Let's order some food.

indian: off the light / on the fan / open the light
natural: turn off the light / turn on the fan / switch on the light
why_en: 'On' and 'off' are not verbs in English. Use 'turn on/off' or 'switch on/off'. 'Open/close' are for doors and windows.
why_hi: अंग्रेज़ी में 'on' और 'off' क्रिया नहीं हैं। 'Turn on/off' या 'switch on/off' कहें। 'Open/close' दरवाज़ों-खिड़कियों के लिए हैं।
example_wrong: Please off the AC and open the light.
example_right: Please turn off the AC and turn on the light.

natural: take an exam / sit an exam
why_en: Students take exams; teachers give them. 'I gave my exam' means you were the examiner.
why_hi: छात्र exam 'take' करते हैं; शिक्षक 'give' करते हैं। 'I gave my exam' का मतलब है आप परीक्षक थे।
example_wrong: I gave my certification exam last week.
example_right: I took my certification exam last week.

natural: killing time / just hanging out / for fun
why_en: 'Timepass' does not exist in English. Depending on meaning: 'just killing time', 'for fun', or 'a time-waster'.
why_hi: 'Timepass' अंग्रेज़ी में नहीं है। अर्थ के अनुसार: 'just killing time', 'for fun', या 'a time-waster'।
example_wrong: That movie was just timepass.
example_right: That movie was fun but forgettable.

natural: you're welcome / don't mention it / no problem
why_en: The English idiom is 'don't mention it'. 'Mention not' reverses the word order and sounds unnatural.
why_hi: अंग्रेज़ी मुहावरा 'don't mention it' है। 'Mention not' शब्द-क्रम उलट देता है और अस्वाभाविक लगता है।
example_wrong: A: Thanks for the help. B: Mention not.
example_right: A: Thanks for the help. B: You're welcome.

natural: hometown / where I'm from
why_en: 'Native place' is Indian English. Native speakers say 'hometown' or 'where I'm from originally'.
why_hi: 'Native place' भारतीय अंग्रेज़ी है। अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले 'hometown' या 'where I'm from originally' कहते हैं।
example_wrong: My native place is Rajkot.
example_right: My hometown is Rajkot. / I'm originally from Rajkot.

natural: classmate / someone from my year / cohort
why_en: 'Batchmate' is understood in India but not elsewhere. Say 'we were in the same year at university'.
why_hi: 'Batchmate' भारत में समझा जाता है लेकिन बाहर नहीं। कहें 'we were in the same year at university'।
example_wrong: He is my batchmate from engineering.
example_right: We were in the same year at engineering college.

natural: eraser
why_en: In American English 'rubber' is slang for a condom. Use 'eraser' to be safe everywhere; 'rubber' is understood in the UK only.
why_hi: अमेरिकी अंग्रेज़ी में 'rubber' कंडोम के लिए बोलचाल का शब्द है। हर जगह सुरक्षित रहने के लिए 'eraser' कहें; 'rubber' सिर्फ़ UK में समझा जाता है।
example_wrong: Can I borrow your rubber?
example_right: Can I borrow your eraser?

natural: skip a class / cut class
why_en: 'Bunk off' exists in British slang but 'bunk a class' is Indian English. 'Skip' is universally clear.
why_hi: ब्रिटिश बोलचाल में 'bunk off' है लेकिन 'bunk a class' भारतीय अंग्रेज़ी है। 'Skip' हर जगह स्पष्ट है।
example_wrong: We bunked the lecture and went for a movie.
example_right: We skipped the lecture and went to see a film.

indian: itself / only (for emphasis: 'I told you only')
natural: (use stress or restructure): I did tell you / I told you myself / right here
why_en: Hindi 'ही' has no single English equivalent. 'Only' at the end of a sentence or 'itself' after a time sounds foreign. Use stress on the verb or 'right' + place/time.
why_hi: हिंदी 'ही' का कोई एक अंग्रेज़ी शब्द नहीं है। वाक्य के अंत में 'only' या समय के बाद 'itself' विदेशी लगता है। क्रिया पर ज़ोर दें या 'right' + जगह/समय कहें।
example_wrong: I will come today itself. I told you only.
example_right: I'll come today. I did tell you.

natural: isn't it? / right? / don't you?
why_en: 'Na' is Hindi. English uses matching tag questions (it's ready, isn't it?) or the informal 'right?'.
why_hi: 'Na' हिंदी है। अंग्रेज़ी में मेल खाते tag question (it's ready, isn't it?) या अनौपचारिक 'right?' आता है।
example_wrong: The build is done, na?
example_right: The build is done, right? / The build is done, isn't it?

natural: I'm sleepy / I'm getting sleepy
why_en: A literal translation of 'नींद आ रही है'. In English, sleepiness is an adjective state, not something that arrives.
why_hi: 'नींद आ रही है' का शाब्दिक अनुवाद। अंग्रेज़ी में उनींदापन एक विशेषण स्थिति है, कुछ ऐसा नहीं जो 'आता' है।
example_wrong: Sleep is coming, I will talk tomorrow.
example_right: I'm getting sleepy — let's talk tomorrow.

natural: my best / everything I can
why_en: 'Do my level best' is dated and mainly Indian. 'I'll do my best' is what native speakers say.
why_hi: 'Do my level best' पुराना और मुख्यतः भारतीय है। अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले 'I'll do my best' कहते हैं।
example_wrong: I will try my level best to finish.
example_right: I'll do my best to finish.

natural: fancy / high-end / posh
why_en: 'Hi-fi' in English means high-fidelity audio equipment. For an expensive restaurant or lifestyle say 'fancy' or 'upmarket'.
why_hi: अंग्रेज़ी में 'hi-fi' का मतलब हाई-फ़िडेलिटी ऑडियो उपकरण है। महँगे रेस्तराँ या जीवनशैली के लिए 'fancy' या 'upmarket' कहें।
example_wrong: They went to a hi-fi restaurant.
example_right: They went to a fancy restaurant.

natural: a hundred percent / completely / absolutely
why_en: 'Cent percent' is Indian English. Native speakers say 'a hundred percent' or '100%'.
why_hi: 'Cent percent' भारतीय अंग्रेज़ी है। अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले 'a hundred percent' या '100%' कहते हैं।
example_wrong: I am cent percent sure it was patched.
example_right: I'm a hundred percent sure it was patched.

natural: one of my friends / a friend of mine
why_en: 'One of' must be followed by a plural: one of my friends. Or use 'a friend of mine'.
why_hi: 'One of' के बाद बहुवचन आना चाहिए: one of my friends। या 'a friend of mine' कहें।
example_wrong: One of my friend works at Google.
example_right: One of my friends works at Google. / A friend of mine works at Google.

natural: I didn't know
why_en: After 'did/didn't' the main verb goes back to its base form. The past is carried by 'did'.
why_hi: 'Did/didn't' के बाद मुख्य क्रिया मूल रूप में आती है। भूतकाल 'did' में पहले से मौजूद है।
example_wrong: I didn't knew about the deadline.
example_right: I didn't know about the deadline.

natural: he has two cars
why_en: 'Have' meaning possess is a state verb and is not used in the continuous. 'Having' is only for actions: having lunch, having a shower.
why_hi: स्वामित्व के अर्थ में 'have' एक स्थिति क्रिया है और continuous में नहीं आती। 'Having' सिर्फ़ क्रियाओं के लिए: having lunch, having a shower।
example_wrong: He is having two cars and a bike.
example_right: He has two cars and a bike.

indian: we are staying here since 5 years
natural: we have been living here for 5 years
why_en: Two fixes: duration from the past to now needs the present perfect (have been), and a length of time takes 'for', not 'since'. 'Since' is for a start point (since 2019).
why_hi: दो सुधार: अतीत से अब तक की अवधि के लिए present perfect (have been) चाहिए, और समय की लंबाई के साथ 'for' आता है, 'since' नहीं। 'Since' शुरुआती बिंदु के लिए है (since 2019)।
example_wrong: I am working in this company since 3 years.
example_right: I have been working at this company for 3 years.

natural: I agree
why_en: 'Agree' is a verb, not an adjective. You don't need 'am'. (Compare: 'I am interested' — adjective.)
why_hi: 'Agree' क्रिया है, विशेषण नहीं। 'Am' की ज़रूरत नहीं। (तुलना करें: 'I am interested' — विशेषण।)
example_wrong: I am agree with your point.
example_right: I agree with your point.

natural: please let me know / please inform me
why_en: 'Intimate' as a verb meaning 'inform' is formal, rare, and mostly Indian. As an adjective it means 'very close/private', which can cause awkwardness.
why_hi: 'Inform' के अर्थ में क्रिया 'intimate' औपचारिक, दुर्लभ और मुख्यतः भारतीय है। विशेषण के रूप में इसका मतलब 'बहुत क़रीबी/निजी' है, जिससे असहजता हो सकती है।
example_wrong: Please intimate me once the server is up.
example_right: Please let me know once the server is up.

natural: can I ask you something? / quick question:
why_en: A translation of 'एक बात बताओ'. In English it can sound like a demand. 'Quick question' or 'Can I ask you something?' is friendlier.
why_hi: 'एक बात बताओ' का अनुवाद। अंग्रेज़ी में यह माँग जैसा लग सकता है। 'Quick question' या 'Can I ask you something?' ज़्यादा दोस्ताना है।
example_wrong: Tell me one thing, is the patch tested?
example_right: Quick question — has the patch been tested?

natural: a 'good enough' attitude / a casual attitude / letting things slide
why_en: Hindi phrase with no single English equivalent. Describe it: 'a good-enough attitude' or 'letting things slide'.
why_hi: हिंदी वाक्यांश जिसका कोई एक अंग्रेज़ी समकक्ष नहीं है। इसे समझाएँ: 'a good-enough attitude' या 'letting things slide'।
example_wrong: The team has a chalta hai attitude about security.
example_right: The team has a 'good enough' attitude about security — they let things slide.

indian: I will be there in some time
natural: I'll be there in a bit / in about 20 minutes / shortly
why_en: 'In some time' is vague and unnatural. Give an estimate or use 'in a bit', 'shortly', 'soon'.
why_hi: 'In some time' अस्पष्ट और अस्वाभाविक है। अनुमान दें या 'in a bit', 'shortly', 'soon' कहें।
example_wrong: I will join the call in some time.
example_right: I'll join the call in about ten minutes.

natural: don't worry / don't stress about it
why_en: 'Take tension' is a Hindi calque ('टेंशन लेना'). English uses 'worry' or 'stress'; 'tension' is not something you take.
why_hi: 'Take tension' हिंदी 'टेंशन लेना' का अनुवाद है। अंग्रेज़ी में 'worry' या 'stress' आता है; 'tension' कोई 'लेने' की चीज़ नहीं है।
example_wrong: Don't take tension, it will be fixed.
example_right: Don't worry, it'll be fixed.

natural: reply to me / explain it to me
why_en: 'Reply' and 'explain' cannot take a person as a direct object. 'Reply to me', 'explain it to me'.
why_hi: 'Reply' और 'explain' के बाद सीधे व्यक्ति नहीं आ सकता। 'Reply to me', 'explain it to me' कहें।
example_wrong: Please reply me and explain me the issue.
example_right: Please reply to me and explain the issue to me.

indian: as per / as per my knowledge
natural: according to / as far as I know
why_en: 'As per' is acceptable in legal or formal writing but overused in Indian English. 'According to' or 'as far as I know' sounds natural.
why_hi: 'As per' क़ानूनी या औपचारिक लेखन में स्वीकार्य है लेकिन भारतीय अंग्रेज़ी में ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा इस्तेमाल होता है। 'According to' या 'as far as I know' स्वाभाविक लगता है।
example_wrong: As per my knowledge, the port is closed.
example_right: As far as I know, the port is closed.
